question: What official action grants a qualified practitioner legal permission to practice their profession?
explanation: Licensing provides the specific legal authority required to deliver healthcare services within a given jurisdiction. [learn more](GST322_U4_T10#GST322_U4_T10_h1)

question: Why is entry into an official database necessary before professional practice begins?

options.A: It exempts the provider from paying professional taxes.
options.B: It sets the salary scale for the newly qualified worker.
options.C: It confirms the basic educational credentials of the practitioner.
options.D: It guarantees immediate employment in a public hospital.

explanation: Registration verifies that an individual has completed approved training and meets baseline standards before entering the workforce. [learn more](GST322_U4_T10#GST322_U4_T10_h1)

question: Which statutory body regulates the education and practice of nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the specific statutory agency empowered by law to control nursing education and professional discipline in Nigeria. [learn more](GST322_U4_T10#GST322_U4_T10_h2)

question: What is the primary function of state-level health facility monitoring agencies?

options.A: Producing drugs for local government clinics
options.B: Inspecting and accrediting physical healthcare premises
options.C: Setting international health treaties for the country
options.D: Conducting national licensing exams for doctors

explanation: State agencies like HEFAMAA focus on ensuring hospitals and clinics meet environmental and facility standards. [learn more](GST322_U4_T10#GST322_U4_T10_h2)

question: What is the primary goal of healthcare provider licensure?
explanation: Licensure acts as a protective barrier to ensure that only competent individuals provide patient care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T10#GST322_U4_T10_h3)

question: A regulatory council revokes a nurse's practicing license due to gross professional misconduct. Which objective does this action primarily fulfill?

options.B: Ensuring professional accountability and protecting patients
options.C: Reducing the number of unemployed healthcare workers
options.D: Lowering the cost of hospital administration

explanation: Revoking licenses removes unsafe practitioners from the field, upholding accountability and protecting the public. [learn more](GST322_U4_T10#GST322_U4_T10_h3)

question: What document must an applicant submit first to begin the licensing process?

options.A: A letter of recommendation from a politician
options.C: Proof of graduation from an accredited institution
options.D: A certificate of tax clearance for five years

explanation: Graduation from an approved training program is the foundational requirement before sitting for board examinations. [learn more](GST322_U4_T10#GST322_U4_T10_h4)

question: What action is required annually to keep a professional healthcare license active in Nigeria?

options.A: Writing the board examination a second time
options.B: Payment of periodic practicing fees and fulfilling continuous education
options.C: Submitting a new nursing diploma to the ministry
options.D: Changing place of employment every twelve months

explanation: Active licenses depend on maintaining good standing through regular fee renewals and professional development. [learn more](GST322_U4_T10#GST322_U4_T10_h4)

question: Why do regulatory boards conduct unannounced inspections of healthcare facilities?

options.A: To distribute free medical supplies to the facility
options.B: To observe normal, everyday operational compliance and safety standards
options.C: To collect annual taxes on behalf of the federal government
options.D: To recruit new nursing students for training schools

explanation: Unannounced visits prevent facilities from staging temporary improvements just for scheduled inspections. [learn more](GST322_U4_T10#GST322_U4_T10_h5)

question: What consequence typically follows when a clinic repeatedly fails regulatory quality standards?

options.C: Sanctions ranging from fines to facility closure
options.D: Automatic promotion of the head nurse

explanation: Severe or repeated non-compliance endangers patients and results in legal penalties or shutdown. [learn more](GST322_U4_T10#GST322_U4_T10_h5)

question: What is a major factor that hinders effective healthcare enforcement in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: Shortage of regulatory personnel and underfunding
options.B: Advanced digital tracking of all clinics
options.C: Excessive number of licensed medical doctors

explanation: Limited resources prevent regulatory councils from adequately patrolling and inspecting remote areas. [learn more](GST322_U4_T10#GST322_U4_T10_h6)

question: Why does the presence of unregistered clinics pose a severe threat to public health?

options.A: They consume most of the drugs meant for teaching hospitals.
options.B: They pay higher taxes than government-owned hospitals.
options.C: They operate without proven competence or standard safety protocols.
options.D: They force licensed professionals to lower their service fees.

explanation: Quacks lack verified training, leading to misdiagnoses, dangerous treatments, and increased patient mortality. [learn more](GST322_U4_T10#GST322_U4_T10_h6)
